generations.memory_31: For SMBs, simplifying signup is a validated way to improve acquisition and activation: signup increased 15%, activation 9%, and qualified revenue 4%, while 30-day retention was essentially flat (-1%). Do not generalize this result beyond SMBs.
generations.memory_44: For enterprise, a sales-assisted CTA can trade lower signup volume for higher lead quality and revenue: signups fell 12%, but qualified leads rose 24% and qualified revenue 18%, with no change in 30-day retention. This is validated only for enterprise.
generations.memory_57: Referral incentives are effective for established accounts, particularly those older than six months: referral starts increased 21%, qualified revenue 7%, and 30-day retention 2%. Target mature accounts rather than applying this broadly.
generations.memory_73: Targeted 40% discounts can produce short-term acquisition and revenue gains among price-sensitive SMBs—signup rose 31% and qualified revenue 18%—but materially weaken cohort quality: 30-day retention fell 12%, and the cohort did not survive the first renewal cycle. Do not use targeted discounting as a sustainable-growth strategy.
generations.memory_86: Shortening onboarding is a validated lever for faster and more durable customer progress: completion increased 13%, time-to-value improved by 2.1 days, and 30-day retention rose 3%.
generations.memory_91: In-product activation messaging is a validated engagement and activation lever: week-one engagement increased 11%, activation 6%, and 30-day retention 1%. Expect a modest retention effect relative to the activation gains.
